clue.text: Honourable position at university in the north

indicators.note: in a down clue the northern piece sits at the top, so these letters come first

parts.note: being up means in residence at a university, as at Oxford or Cambridge
one's standing is one's position or rank

explanation.surface: Someone holds an honourable post at a northern university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the north' reads as geography but places the university piece above the other in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstanding person is honest and respectable, a close synonym of honourable.

clue.text: Pernickety poet finally coming to the fore in film

indicators.note: the reworked poet sits inside the film word

parts.note: pic is informal for a film or picture

indicators.note: the poet's final letter moves from the back to the front

parts.note: Dante Alighieri, the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: A fussy poet at last takes the lead role in a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally coming to the fore' moves the last E of DANTE to the front, giving EDANT, which goes 'in' PIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedantic means overly concerned with minor details, which is what a pernickety person is.

clue.text: Half-hearted measures adopted by state security

indicators.note: taken in by, so the trimmed measures go inside

parts.note: to state something is to say it

indicators.note: the word's heart is the pair EE; losing half of it leaves one

parts.note: feet are units of length, so measures

explanation.surface: A government takes half-hearted steps over national security.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-hearted' removes one of the two middle Es of FEET, leaving FET, which is 'adopted by' SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Safety and security are synonyms: both mean freedom from danger.

clue.text: Current speaker's restrained

indicators.note: what a speaker says is heard, so a word that is pronounced the same

parts.note: tied up, held back by bonds

explanation.surface: A public speaker's current remarks are rather restrained.
explanation.definitionFit: A tide is a current of sea water flowing in or out.

clue.text: Expect head to support worker here in Paris

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting piece sits beneath the others

parts.note: a worker ant is the crossword's stock worker
ici is French for here
pate is an old word for the head

explanation.surface: A French boss is expected to back up an employee here.
explanation.definitionFit: To anticipate is to expect or look ahead to something happening.

clue.text: Band cut up, admitting source of recent infection

parts.note: a ring is a circular band

indicators.note: letting in, so the cut word holds the next letter
in a down entry, up means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: to mow is to cut grass

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A band split up after a recent infection went round the members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns MOW into WOM, which is 'admitting' R from 'source of recent' to give WORM.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringworm is a contagious fungal skin infection, named for its ring-shaped rash.

clue.text: Brown well beaten

explanation.definitionFit: Tanned means sun-browned, and to tan someone's hide is to give them a beating.

clue.text: Single swimmer's base

definitions.meaning: a flatfish found off European coasts
the underside of a foot or shoe

explanation.surface: An unmarried swimmer has a base of operations.
explanation.definitionFit: Sole means only, is a flatfish, and is the underside of the foot: three separate senses.

clue.text: Editor stops "helping" on page, so the Eagle survives

indicators.note: plugs, so the editor goes inside the helping

parts.note: a ration is a portion or helping

explanation.surface: An editor withholds a handout on the page so the Eagle comic can stay afloat.
explanation.walkthrough: The Eagle reads as the boys' comic, but it is a bird of prey that lives by hunting.
explanation.definitionFit: Predation is hunting and killing other animals for food, which is how an eagle stays alive.

clue.text: State promise in church to secure a husband

indicators.note: holding something firmly, so the vow surrounds the other letters

parts.note: the wedding vow spoken at the altar
H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogies

explanation.surface: A church wedding vow is made in order to land a husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the states of the USA, in the north-west.

clue.text: Bar on which artists depend

parts.note: circus performers hang from this swinging bar; 'depend' in its literal sense of hanging down

explanation.surface: Performers rely on a certain drinking venue for their living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depend' seems to mean rely on, but it means hang from, and the bar is a pole, not a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus swing is a horizontal bar hung on ropes from which acrobats literally hang.

clue.text: Artless miss, say, retreating in tavern used regularly

indicators.note: the reversed letters sit inside the tavern word

parts.note: an inn is a tavern

indicators.note: going backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: EG, for example, is what 'say' means in a clue

indicators.note: every other letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: An innocent young woman, say, backs away in a pub that is used often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' turns EG into GE, placed 'in' INN; 'used regularly' gives U and E.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingenue is an innocent, unsophisticated young woman, especially as a stock stage role.

clue.text: Smart races, no outdated fences

indicators.note: encloses, so the old no surrounds the races

parts.note: nay is an old-fashioned word for no
TT, the Tourist Trophy motorcycle races on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Smart races no longer use old-fashioned fences.
explanation.definitionFit: Natty means smartly and neatly dressed.

clue.text: How crusaders acquired their protection?

parts.note: medieval knights wore chain armour, so it is imagined being ordered by post

explanation.surface: A historical question about how crusaders got their armour.
explanation.walkthrough: Chain mail is the armour; the joke makes its purchase a postal-catalogue transaction.
explanation.definitionFit: Mail order is buying goods by post, and crusaders' protection was literally mail.

clue.text: Believer for whom the motion's turbulent?

indicators.note: in turmoil, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the S of the possessive is used as a letter here

explanation.surface: A believer for whom a debate's motion causes uproar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turbulent' rearranges THE MOTIONS; the clue also hints at a believer in one god for whom motion is stirred.
explanation.definitionFit: A monotheist is one who believes in a single god, a specific kind of believer.

clue.text: Butcher (not I) docking rear part of grounds

indicators.note: to butcher something is to hack it about, so the letters are mangled
leave out, so the letter is removed from the fodder

parts.note: the letter I, taken as written

explanation.surface: A butcher, not me, docks the rear of an animal on the estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not I' removes the I from DOCKING; 'Butcher' then rearranges DOCKNG plus REAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A rock garden is a section of a garden or grounds laid out with stones and alpine plants.

clue.text: Background notes including medical units rewritten

parts.note: inc. is the short form of including

indicators.note: written out again, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Background notes that include medical units have been redrafted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Background notes' looks like a written briefing, but the notes are musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Incidental music is played in the background of a film or play, so it is background notes in the musical sense.

clue.text: Stop sending up assistance — clergyman's run off

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means read bottom to top

parts.note: aid is help or assistance

indicators.note: gone away, so the letter leaves the word

parts.note: a parson is a clergyman; the 's stands for has
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Stop sending aid to the vicar: he has run off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sending up' turns AID into DIA; PARSON with R 'off' leaves PASON.
explanation.definitionFit: A diapason is a principal organ stop, so a stop in the organ-building sense.

clue.text: Fighter who's put out about amateur

indicators.note: around, so the rearranged letters surround the amateur
put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored and its letters are used

explanation.surface: A boxer who has been knocked out by an amateur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges WHOS and PUT into SOUTHPW, which goes 'about' A.
explanation.definitionFit: A southpaw is a left-handed boxer, so a kind of fighter.

clue.text: Bond's nature changed with age

indicators.note: altered, so the letters are put in another order

explanation.surface: James Bond's character altered as he grew older.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests 007, but it is a pledge or surety.
explanation.definitionFit: A bond is a binding promise or security, the same thing as a pledge that something will be done.

clue.text: Worried about zealot's rising temper …

indicators.note: around, so the worry word surrounds the other

parts.note: something that ate at you worried you

indicators.note: going up a down entry, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a nut is a fanatic; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious about a fanatic's growing anger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns NUT into TUN, which ATE goes 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: To temper or tune an instrument is to bring it into harmony, which is what attuning does.

clue.text: Fleeced animals from Africa moving west over time

indicators.note: covering, so the turned word goes round the time letter
in an across entry, west is leftwards, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: gnus are African antelopes

explanation.surface: Sheared wildebeest migrate west as time passes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving west' turns GNUS into SUNG, which goes 'over' T after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Stung is slang for overcharged or swindled, just as fleeced is.

clue.text: … religion thus riven by suspicion

indicators.note: split apart by, so the second piece goes inside

parts.note: so means thus, in this way
a hint is a trace or suspicion of something

explanation.surface: A faith is torn apart by mistrust.
explanation.definitionFit: Shinto is the indigenous religion of Japan.

clue.text: Gunners drop unremitting quest for success

parts.note: the RA, Royal Artillery
a trace is a tiny amount, a drop

explanation.surface: Artillerymen abandon a relentless pursuit of victory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drop' looks like a verb, but it is a noun meaning a tiny amount.
explanation.definitionFit: The rat race is the endless competitive struggle to get ahead in work and life.

clue.text: Birds dropping in sacks

indicators.note: letting fall, so these letters are taken out

parts.note: robins are birds

explanation.surface: Birds are letting droppings fall into sacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacks' looks like bags, but it is a verb meaning plunders.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack a town is to plunder it, so sacks and robs are synonyms.

clue.text: How the legless proceed and possibly buttonhole the lady?

parts.note: a buttonhole is a slit in fabric
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: How drunks stagger along, perhaps accosting a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legless' is British slang for very drunk, and buttonhole means to accost; in fact they are snakes, and a slit.
explanation.definitionFit: Snakes and other limbless creatures move by sliding along the ground.

clue.text: Tonics set up in Boots, maybe

indicators.note: put upward in a down entry, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: doh is the tonic note in sol-fa

explanation.surface: Health tonics are displayed at Boots, the British chain of chemist shops.
explanation.walkthrough: Boots is a British high-street chemist; here it is footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Shod means wearing shoes or other footwear, such as boots.

clue.text: Something to play during suburban journey

indicators.note: within the span of, so the answer lies inside these words

explanation.surface: A game or toy to pass the time on a commuter trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A banjo is a stringed instrument, something one plays.

clue.text: Type of radio broadcast lacking signal?

parts.note: short of something means lacking it
a wave is a hand signal

explanation.surface: A radio transmission with no signal to carry it.
explanation.definitionFit: Short wave is a band of radio frequencies used for long-distance broadcasting.
